projects.title: Third Places NYC
projects.description: Interactive map by James Piacentini of roughly 10,400 community gathering spots across the five boroughs -- cafes, bars, libraries, parks, and community centers -- each tagged with machine-generated 'soul summaries' and community-identity labels. Spotlighted in BetaNYC's July 2 civic-tech roundup.
projects.why_interesting: Applies the sociological 'third place' concept to a citywide map and uses ML to describe the social character of each spot -- a fresh take on mapping the informal social fabric rather than infrastructure.

projects.title: NYC Performance Tracker (Mayor's Management Report dashboard)
projects.description: Dashboard by Ted Alcorn aggregating Mayor's Management Report metrics from 1998 to present, letting users explore agency performance and neighborhood-level indicators across more than 25 years in one interface. Featured in BetaNYC's June 25 roundup.
projects.why_interesting: The MMR is normally buried in annual PDFs; putting a quarter-century of city performance data behind a single explorer is a rare longitudinal view of how agencies actually perform.

projects.title: Apartment Audit NYC
projects.description: Consumer tool built on NYC Open Data that helps renters navigate Department of Buildings and Housing Preservation and Development records more accessibly than the city's own portals, surfacing violations and complaints for a given address.
projects.why_interesting: A resident-facing wrapper that turns the city's clunky DOB and HPD data into something a prospective tenant can actually use -- civic data reframed as consumer protection.

projects.title: NYC Community Health Profiles
projects.description: Health Department tool serving neighborhood-level profiles with more than 50 health measures per area, spotlighted in BetaNYC's July 2 civic-tech roundup.
projects.why_interesting: Neighborhood-scale health data in one place is a durable reference for anyone reporting on inequities across NYC's community districts.

projects.title: Citizenry NYC
projects.description: Discovery platform that connects New Yorkers to civic organizations, programs, and local participation opportunities, featured in BetaNYC's June 25 roundup.
projects.why_interesting: Tackles the discovery gap in civic life -- most residents never learn what programs or community groups exist near them; this is an attempt to index that landscape.

projects.title: NYC Summer Programs Guide
projects.description: Searchable city tool for finding youth summer programming by age, ZIP code, and interest, spotlighted in BetaNYC's July 2 roundup amid the summer enrollment push.
projects.why_interesting: A seasonal example of the city consolidating a fragmented resource landscape into one searchable interface -- the same pattern seen in the child-care map earlier this year.

projects.title: NYC Urban Heat Portal
projects.description: BetaNYC visualization portal tracking urban heat patterns across NYC neighborhoods, re-featured in the late-June and July civic-tech roundups as the first heat wave of the summer hit.
projects.why_interesting: Heat is New York's deadliest weather hazard; a neighborhood-level heat map is exactly the kind of tool that gets timely each July.

projects.title: Hudson Link Reliability Dashboard
projects.description: Web app tracking reliability failures on the Hudson Link commuter bus system serving the lower Hudson Valley, surfaced in BetaNYC's June 25 civic-tech roundup.
projects.why_interesting: Rider-built accountability for a suburban transit service that gets far less data scrutiny than the MTA -- a template for holding smaller transit operators to account.

projects.title: Brockovich Data Center Map
projects.description: Crowdsourced map documenting AI data center construction across the country, tracking energy and water use and siting concerns, featured in BetaNYC's June 25 roundup.
projects.why_interesting: Community-sourced mapping of the data-center buildout -- a bottom-up counter to industry secrecy on where these energy- and water-hungry facilities are landing.

projects.title: San Diego modern Open Data Portal
projects.description: San Diego relaunched its Open Data Portal on June 4, 2026 with more than 100 datasets -- Get It Done service reports, street repairs, transit routes, short-term rental licenses, traffic collisions, and hate-crime reports -- plus plain-language search and premade dashboards.
projects.why_interesting: A full portal overhaul that leans into natural-language search and prebuilt dashboards -- a look at where municipal open-data platforms are heading in the AI era.

projects.title: Prince William County Data Center Map
projects.description: Interactive map launched in June 2026 showing data center projects at every stage of development, with pop-ups detailing acreage, square footage, zoning classification, and case numbers, delivered through County Mapper and a build-out analysis dashboard.
projects.why_interesting: One of the first county governments to proactively map its own data-center pipeline for the public -- a transparency model for the many localities now wrestling with data-center sprawl.

projects.title: Civic Tech World Cup
projects.description: Bracket-style voting platform from the Civic Tech Field Guide that pits real civic-tech projects against each other in knockout rounds, with readers voting favorites forward. Running through summer 2026.
projects.why_interesting: A playful discovery mechanism for the sprawling global civic-tech catalog -- a way to surface tools that would otherwise stay buried in a directory.
